Consult Summary:
- Adult male with 3-day history of watery diarrhea (6–7/day) and intermittent left lower abdominal cramping, with initial vomiting and subjective fever at onset; able to maintain fluids; no blood in stool or emesis.
- Clinical impression: likely acute gastroenteritis after recent takeaway meal; conservative management advised with oral rehydration, paracetamol, rest, and follow-up if not improved in 3–4 days.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute diarrhea with abdominal cramps (likely gastroenteritis)
  - Onset/duration: 3 days.
  - Symptoms: watery/loose stools 6–7 times/day; intermittent crampy left lower abdominal pain; initial vomiting now resolved; felt hot/subjective fever at onset (3–4 days ago); weakness/shaky; reduced appetite; able to keep fluids down; eating soups/smooth foods.
  - Pertinent negatives: no blood in stools; no blood in vomit; denies night sweats; no current fever reported; pain does not radiate to back.
  - Exposure: ate takeaway (Chinese restaurant) 4 days ago; one child vomited but no diarrhea; no similar symptoms reported in others at home.
  - Examination: not documented.
  - Impression: acute gastroenteritis (viral most likely; bacterial possible).
  - Management advised: oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte), maintain hydration and light diet; paracetamol as needed; rest and time off work 2–3 days; review if not improved in 3–4 days; stool testing if persistent.

Issue 2:
- Asthma (well-controlled)
  - History: longstanding asthma; uses an inhaler; no current respiratory complaints.
  - Medications: inhaler (type and regimen not documented).
  - Plan: continue usual inhaler (no changes documented).

Issue 3:
- Occupational impact due to acute illness
  - Patient has continued working as an accountant despite frequent diarrhea; needs proximity to toilet; advised to take 2–3 days off work to rest and recover.

Medications:
- Asthma inhaler — dose/route/frequency not documented; type not documented.
- Paracetamol — “two tablets up to four times daily” (strength/route not documented), short term for fever/aches.
- Dioralyte (oral rehydration salts) — dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- Not documented.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma (well-controlled).

Social History:
- Lives with wife and two children.
- Occupation: Accountant.
- Non-smoker.
- Does not drink alcohol.

Preventative History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: not documented.
- Examination findings: not performed/documented.

Plan:
- Conservative management for presumed gastroenteritis: maintain hydration; use oral rehydration solution; light diet as tolerated.
- Paracetamol as advised for fever/aches.
- Rest; take 2–3 days off work.
- Follow up if symptoms not improving within 3–4 days; consider stool testing if persistent.
- No antibiotics at this stage.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: drug allergies; medication reconciliation with doses/strengths; vitals; physical exam; recent travel, recent antibiotics, and red-flag symptom review (e.g., severe dehydration) not fully documented.
- Internal conflicts: When asked about vomiting, patient initially said “no,” then clarified vomiting occurred at symptom onset but has since resolved (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor repetitions and brief ambiguities but adequate for documentation.
